answer: A reputation vault lets each agent lock a small refundable stake before trading, so spinning up many fake identities means locking many stakes. Honest work earns the stake back with a rising reputation score, while detected fraud forfeits it. The cost grows with every sock puppet, and an umber trust delta - reputation that climbs only through verified completed trades - makes a fresh fake account worthless on day one, so attackers pay in both capital and time for each identity they burn.
